title: Knowledge check: Route Parameters

questions.prompt: Which source-syllabus topic is explicitly covered by “Route Parameters”?
options: Flask's purpose in Python web development
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Dynamic URL segments” under lesson 20, “Route Parameters”. Keep this subtopic aligned to its module and confirm version-sensitive details in the official Flask documentation.

questions.prompt: When applying “Route Parameters” in a real Flask application, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Trust the browser and skip server-side checks.
Change several parts at once and infer success from one happy-path request.
Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
Expose internal tracebacks to the caller to simplify debugging.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
questions.explanation: For route parameters, use the matching official documentation, a narrow example, and a test of both normal and invalid conditions. Browser validation alone and exposed tracebacks are not reliable safeguards.

questions.prompt: Which design principle best complements “Route Parameters” as the course moves toward production?
options: Assume Flask automatically provides a database, authentication system and task queue.
Treat a development server or debug mode as the production deployment plan.
Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
Assume a green diagram proves correctness without running a test.
questions.answer_key: Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Flask is a lightweight framework whose databases, account management, caching and task queues commonly come from separately selected tools. Verify trust boundaries and runtime assumptions with tests.
